implementation_notes: Ruby's Rails shape makes this smell very common: a helper that builds a display string from an ActiveRecord object (`order.ship_to.city`), or a `before_save` callback that computes something from a related record. Rails offers a partial structural answer — value objects (`ActiveModel::Type::Value` or plain POROs) that the model exposes as an attribute — which lets the rule live on the value while the column stays on the model. Otherwise Move Method in the normal sense.
idiom_name: view helper / model method reading another model’s columns
code_sketch:
class OrdersHelper                    # envious
  def label(order)
    "#{order.status}:#{order.ship_to.city}"
  end
end

# after: on the value that owns the data
class Address
  def label(status) = "#{status}:#{city}"
end
pitfalls: A helper that formats for display is doing the view's job, and the view is the right home for presentation formatting even though it reads the model's data.
Delegated associations (`order.customer.name`) inside a scope are query composition, not a misplaced rule.
Putting domain rules on a Rails model and a presentation format on a helper is the actual split; putting both on the model is the other half of the smell.
